subject: Re: Territory escrow & transient egress questions for DPA redline
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acmehealth.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Territory escrow & transient egress questions for DPA redline

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking a look at our DPA redline. A few items came up during our security review that we need clarified before we can move to procurement: 

1) Temporary cross-border failover windows — we see notes in the DPA about transient processing outside the primary territory for disaster recovery and maintenance. Can you confirm what the maximum window is you can commit to (we're trying to avoid anything open-ended)? Is there a policy for automatic notification + post-event audit report?

2) Escrow/escrowed access — our security team asked whether Redwood supports an "escrow" pattern for telemetry/logs or key escrow for forensic requests. We understand key escrow is sensitive, but they want to know what options exist for short-term access with strong audit controls.

3) Subprocessor visibility — please provide the list of subprocessors that could be involved if a transient hop goes to EU/APAC during a failover, and whether those subprocessors have separate DPA agreements.

4) KMS control & re-encryption — if we bring our own keys (BYOK), can transient processing be done without exposing plaintext to Redwood personnel? Is ephemeral re-encryption supported for short windows?

Attached: Acme_DPA_redline_v1.pdf (redlines).

We'd like to get answers in writing so procurement can proceed with the PO. If easier, happy to set a quick call.

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Security Programs
Acme Health

From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Territory escrow & transient egress questions for DPA redline

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Marissa (privacy/ops) to give formal language; Karthik from infra is cc'd for operational details. High-level answers below; Kimberly/Marissa will follow with precise DPA/addendum language.

1) Maximum transient egress window: we can commit to a documented maximum of 72 hours for unplanned failover or DR-triggered transient processing, with a formal post-event report. For planned maintenance we publish scheduled windows in advance and limit per-region maintenance to agreed SLAs. We will add a notification requirement (email + portal notice) within 2 hours of failover and produce an audit bundle within 5 business days.

2) Escrow/escaped access: Redwood does not provide plaintext data escrow to third parties. We can provide escrowed telemetry and encrypted forensic snapshots (with metadata) under NDA. If Acme requires data escrow, we can propose a narrow-scope automated export (encrypted) to an Acme-controlled bucket for the transient window — this would be a contractual addendum and is operationally feasible.

3) Subprocessor visibility: see the attached geo-egress-playbook.xlsx — it contains the roster of cloud and infra subprocessors by region and their DPA status. Short answer: EU failover may involve our EU cloud partner (listed) and an edge CDN provider; APAC failover involves our APAC infra partner. All subprocessors handling customer data are on DPA terms; we can provide signed copies for any names you need.

4) KMS + ephemeral re-encryption: we support BYOK via customer-managed KMS in the supported regions. For transient processing scenarios we support an ephemeral key wrapping flow: data remains encrypted at rest, and tokenized/unwrapped keys are created for ephemeral instances and automatically destroyed after the window. Redwood staff never have access to unwrapped key material in the BYOK flow. We'll include architecture notes for the ephemeral re-encryption process.

Next steps I suggest: Kimberly propose DPA addendum language (72-hour transient window + notification + audit), Marissa share operational runbook and playbook extracts, and then we schedule a 30-minute call with Acme procurement to align on PO language.

Attaching: geo-egress-playbook.xlsx (playbook + subprocessor roster extract).

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acmehealth.com>, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Territory escrow & transient egress questions for DPA redline

Hi Elena — thanks for the redline and the questions. A few legal points and proposed language fragments you can consider adding to the DPA as an addendum: 

• Transient Processing Window: "Customer acknowledges and agrees that Redwood may, on a temporary basis, process Customer Data outside the Customer's designated Territory for the purpose of Disaster Recovery, maintenance, or capacity rebalancing; such transient processing shall not exceed seventy-two (72) consecutive hours per incident without Customer's prior written consent. Redwood shall provide notice to Customer within two (2) hours of the start of any such transient processing event and shall deliver an audit bundle describing the incident and data movements within five (5) business days of cessation."

• Notification & Audit: Add the notification commitment above and require an audit bundle (timestamps, affected model endpoints, egress locations, subprocessors).

• Escrow/Export Option: "Upon Customer request and subject to a separate escrow agreement, Redwood will export encrypted forensic snapshots to a Customer-designated storage location for the duration of an agreed escrow period. Redwood will not hold plaintext copies for escrow purposes."

• Subprocessor representations: include the subprocessor roster reference and confirm that Redwood shall use subprocessors bound by equivalent DPA terms. If Acme wants signed copies, procurement can request them via the HubSpot ticket and Redwood legal will produce signed DPA exhibits for each named subprocessor.

Operational notes: we will not accept an open-ended key-escrow requirement. BYOK + ephemeral wrapping (as described by Priyom) is our recommended path for preserving key control.

If Acme procurement is comfortable with the 72-hour cap and the audit/notification commitments, we can produce a concise addendum for signature this week. Happy to join a call to walk through the exact contractual language.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Priyom and Kimberly — this is very helpful and aligns with what our security team will accept. A couple quick asks before we circulate to procurement: 

- Can you send a short paragraph (one or two sentences) we can paste into our PO language stating the 72-hour transient processing cap and the notification SLA? Procurement prefers copy/pasteable language.
- Procurement would like signed DPA exhibits for any subprocessors involved in EU/APAC failover — please confirm an ETA for those signed copies.

Procurement will prepare a PO draft once we have that paragraph and confirmation on the subprocessor exhibit ETA. Let's tentatively schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to close the DPA addendum.

Best,
Elena
